facts.t: Parliament can redraw a state without its consent
facts.d: Article 3 requires only that the state legislature be given a chance to express its views — and Parliament is not bound by them. Telangana in 2014 and the Jammu and Kashmir reorganisation in 2019 both proceeded on that footing.

facts.t: The Inter-State Council sat unused for four decades
facts.d: Article 263 provided for it in 1950. It was actually constituted only in 1990, on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation. Its meetings since have been sporadic — which is why every reform list asks for it to be revived rather than created.

facts.t: District collectors do not work for the state that posts them
facts.d: All India Services officers under Article 312 are recruited centrally, serve state cadres, and can be recalled to the Union. It is the one administrative structure that makes India's federalism visibly asymmetric at the district level.

bank.q: Consider the following as examples of cooperative federalism:
s: Ease of Doing Business rankings among states.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are cooperative. Ease of Doing Business rankings are the classic instance of competitive federalism — states ranked against one another.

bank.q: Match List I (unitary feature) with List II (constitutional basis):
bank.e: All India Services in Article 312, boundary alteration in Article 3, concurrent supremacy in Article 254, residuary powers in Article 248 with Entry 97.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT an example of confrontational federalism?
bank.e: Ayushman Bharat is cited as cooperative federalism — a jointly funded and jointly implemented programme.

bank.q: The chief risk associated with competitive federalism is:
o: A race to the bottom and widening regional inequality
Erosion of trust leading to constitutional crises
bank.e: States competing on concessions can undercut one another, and stronger states pull further ahead. Coordination delay is the cooperative model's weakness; erosion of trust belongs to the confrontational one.

bank.as: India's Constitution is often described as having a strong unitary spine.
bank.rs: Emergency provisions, All India Services, residuary powers with Parliament and an integrated election and audit machinery all tilt authority towards the Centre.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the accumulation of these features is precisely what led Wheare to call the system quasi-federal.

bank.q: With reference to integrated national machinery, consider the following statements:
s: The Election Commission conducts state assembly elections.
The Comptroller and Auditor General audits state accounts.
Each state maintains its own separate criminal code.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Criminal law is on the Concurrent List and Parliament's codes — the BNS, BNSS and BSA — apply nationwide.

bank.q: All of the following are cited as examples of competitive federalism EXCEPT:
o: Competition among states for foreign direct investment
bank.e: The Inter-State Council is a cooperative institution under Article 263, designed for consultation rather than rivalry.

bank.q: Which article empowers the Union to give directions to states?
bank.e: Articles 256 and 257 oblige states to comply with laws of Parliament and permit Union directions on specified matters.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about financial unitary features:
s: Centrally sponsored schemes come with central guidelines attached to funding.
Cesses and surcharges lie outside the divisible pool.
States can independently borrow abroad without Union approval.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. External borrowing by states requires Union approval — another element of financial dependence.

bank.q: Which of the following best describes the nature of confrontational federalism?
o: A horizontal partnership with shared responsibility
Vertical and horizontal rivalry for development
A vertical relationship where central dominance breeds disputes
bank.e: It is vertical and adversarial, typically triggered by the Centre entering state domains — though it can usefully force judicial clarification of the boundaries.
